evidence_action.first: Pick one part you were responsible for in a design or lab project, and record the reasons behind its dimensions or conditions, along with the values you calculated, in a design drawing and an analysis condition sheet.
evidence_action.next: Test or recalculate that part and compare against the earlier values, then write down in a design change record why any difference exceeded the allowable range and what you changed in the design as a result.

SPEC_ME_MECHATRONICS.name: Mechatronics
SPEC_ME_MECHATRONICS.note: The side that adds sensors and control to mechanical devices to make them move

scene: Choosing motors and sensors that suit the part that has to move
When target motion and actual motion differ, working out whether the mechanism or the control is at fault
Setting the sequence for a repetitive task and the conditions for stopping it
evidence: In a lab course, wiring up motors and sensors and recording what you observed as they moved
In a team project, comparing motors and sensors on their datasheets and choosing which to use
In a capstone, designing the mechanism and circuit together and fixing them through testing
In a lab course, measuring position or vibration to set control values and trying changes
In an internship, recording the conditions and alarms that make automated equipment stop
In a club or competition, building a robot or drone and documenting the part you were responsible for

evidence_action.first: Pick one project where you made a device move, and record the reasons you chose its motors and sensors, along with the control values you tuned the motion with, in a drive selection sheet and a motion test record.
evidence_action.next: Repeat the same motion many times, collect the cases that exceeded the allowable error, decide whether each deviation came from the mechanism or the control, and write it in the motion test record.
evidence_action.note: The material for these tasks comes from that domain's `verify_targets` and `artifacts`. No new material is invented here.

application.resume: In one paragraph, describe one device you built: the basis on which you chose its drive and sensors, and, when the motion went wrong, how far you narrowed down the cause and what you fixed.
interview: What was the basis for choosing those motors and sensors?
When the motion went wrong, which did you look at first, the mechanism or the control?
After the fix, how did you confirm it was moving correctly?
